insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's receipt corpus is generating $84,826 in confirmed 7-day GMV across 1,972 verified transactions — each one a cryptographically confirmed purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM to reach people who might buy, this is the delta: deterministic proof of spend, not probabilistic inference.

insights.topic: Grocery vertical depth and premium signal
insights.insight: Six distinct grocery brands — Walmart, Kroger, Costco, Publix, Whole Foods, and Trader Joe's — are all crossing receipt-count thresholds within the 14-day window, spanning mass-market through premium positioning. Whole Foods carries the highest average ticket of the grocery set, confirming that premium grocery buyers are present and attributable, not just the value segment.

insights.topic: Unknown category as high-value unattributed spend
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category averages $85.59 per receipt versus $45.07 for grocery — nearly double — and accounts for $32,354 of the 14-day GMV pool. This is a persistent structural signal, not noise: a high-spend segment exists in the corpus that has not yet been attributed to a named retail category, representing both a targeting gap and a data enrichment opportunity.

The network has confirmed 19 active CBSA metro cells, with two consecutive UTC-midnight windows each producing multi-cell additions — a pattern that suggests cluster-threshold dynamics tied to the rolloff cycle, not random geographic drift. For brands that require metro-level or regional purchase verification, coverage is actively expanding.

insights.topic: Receipt base maturing: shallower rolloff troughs each cycle
insights.insight: The Nov 26 UTC-midnight rolloff dropped only $6,824 and 199 receipts from the 7-day window, compared to a $12,994 drop in the Nov 24 cycle. Shallower troughs indicate a denser, more recent receipt base surviving each window shift — the corpus is becoming more stable and less dependent on any single cohort of submissions.

insights.topic: Settlement freeze vs. active receipt intake
insights.insight: Payouts have been frozen at 809 total and 15,415,419 sats claimed across the entire observation window, while receipt intake and GMV accumulation continue without interruption. The divergence is structural and unexplained by observable data — brands evaluating this as a live commerce data source should note that the receipt layer is functioning, but the settlement layer is not currently clearing.
